sentences.zh: 它们全都是 Objective-C 写的。

sentences.en: There's like hundreds of these things that come with the SDK.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Swift 内部非常干净利落地使用每一个组件。

sentences.en: They were all objective C.
sentences.zh: 你可以编写——你可以把你庞大的 Objective-C 项目，也就是你已经发布了多年的这款应用，拿过来，

sentences.en: You could use every single one of them very cleanly from within Swift.
sentences.zh: 用 Swift 编写一个单独的新源文件，它就能与你的 Objective-C 代码完美互操作。

sentences.en: You could write, you could take your giant objective
sentences.zh: 所以尝试它没有任何风险。

sentences.en: C project, this app you'd been shipping for, you know, years and write one single new source file in
sentences.zh: 当你看到很多其他语言问世时，你其实看不到这一点。

sentences.en: Swift, and it would interoperate with your objective C cleanly.
sentences.zh: 通常你必须全盘接受一套全新的技术栈、一个全新的软件包生态系统，才能在实际项目中使用该语言。

sentences.en: So there was no risk involved in trying it.
sentences.zh: 我们走了这种细粒度的路线，以便许许多多的人都能够尝试它。

sentences.en: And you don't actually see this with a whole lot of languages when they come out.
sentences.zh: 这样做的好处是，我们获得了大量的反馈。

sentences.en: Like often you have to like really buy in to a whole new stack, a whole new package ecosystem to actually use the language in something.
sentences.zh: 因此我们可以迭代语言、迭代工具、不断改进，在接下来的几年里把它打造成人们心目中的理想语言。

sentences.en: We went this fine grained route so that many, many people were able to try it.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，它是更优秀的语言这一优势，加上一个习惯了变化、习惯了采用新技术的社区，

sentences.en: The great thing about that is we got a ton of feedback.
sentences.zh: 再加上尝试它的成本极低，这些因素结合起来，意味着我们能够相当快地推动人们完成转变。

sentences.en: So we could iterate on the language, iterate on the tools, refine things to make it the language that people wanted it to be over the next couple of years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可能还有一部分原因在于身处一个拥有集中化供应商的生态系统中——

sentences.en: And so I think the combination of it being better, it being a community that is, you know, used to change and used to adopting new technologies.
sentences.zh: Swift 并不是诞生在一个拥有 10 或 12 个不同组织的世界里，不需要所有人共同努力才能使所有框架具备互操作性。

sentences.en: And also the fact that there was very little cost to trying it out meant that we were able to move people pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 这就像是苹果可以做出一个自上而下的决定：嘿，我们需要让它运作起来。

sentences.en: And I mean, I guess probably, I guess a part of it too, is being in an ecosystem with a centralized
sentences.zh: 只有一个组织，它能够某种程度上推动整个平台上的所有工作。

sentences.en: vendor that can, you know, you didn't, Swift didn't exist in a world where there were like
sentences.zh: 如果你想在 Linux 上做到这一点，你就必须跟一大群不同的人沟通，而每个人都有着不同的目标和意图。

sentences.en: 10 or 12 different organizations, all of whom needed to do that work to make all the frameworks interoperable.
sentences.zh: 我认为，要全面推出你所需要的工具、互操作支持和各种保障，难度要大得多。

sentences.en: It was like, that could be like a top-down decision from Apple that, hey, we need to make this work.
sentences.zh: 不需要所有人共同努力才能使所有框架具备互操作性。

sentences.en: And there's one org and that can sort of make the entire work across the entire platform.
sentences.zh: 这就像是苹果可以做出一个自上而下的决定：嘿，我们需要让它运作起来。

sentences.en: You try to do that in Linux and you got to talk to a whole bunch of different people, all of whom have different goals and objectives.
sentences.zh: 只有一个组织，它能够某种程度上推动整个平台上的所有工作。

sentences.en: And it's a lot harder, I think, to roll out, just roll out the tools and the interop and the support that you need to.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在 Linux 上做到这一点，你就必须跟一大群不同的人沟通，而每个人都有着不同的目标和意图。

sentences.en: I think that's largely true.
sentences.zh: 我想这在很大程度上是真的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, we're still in a big organization.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们仍然身处一个庞大的组织中。

sentences.en: So, right.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: And Swift, the interoperability that Swift enjoys with Objective-C is, at least certainly initially, it was entirely based on the way that we designed and built the compiler.
sentences.zh: 而 Swift 与 Objective-C 之间的互操作性，至少在最初阶段，完全是基于我们设计和构建编译器的方式。

sentences.en: So it is a compiler feature that, so Swift, the compiler, embeds the entire Clang compiler in it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个编译器特性，也就是说 Swift 的编译器在内部嵌入了整个 Clang 编译器。

sentences.en: And the way we use a C or Objective-C or C++ library is we parse the headers and the compiler has a mapping
sentences.zh: 我们使用 C、Objective-C 或 C++ 库的方式是解析头文件，并且编译器拥有一个映射机制

sentences.en: from feature X in C and C++ and Objective-C over to the way that Swift would represent that same thing.
sentences.zh: 将 C、C++ 和 Objective-C 中的特性 X 转换成 Swift 表示相同事物的方式。

sentences.en: And then the code generator works along with Clang's code generator to make the API lineup.
sentences.zh: 然后，代码生成器与 Clang 的代码生成器协同工作，使 API 保持一致。

sentences.en: It sounds a lot like what the Carbon project is trying to get out of their interoperability story.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很像 Carbon 项目正试图在其互操作性方案中实现的目标。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how familiar you are with Carbon, but it's the...
sentences.zh: 我不太清楚你对 Carbon 了解多少，但它...

sentences.en: I'm only familiar with their goals and so on.
sentences.zh: 我只了解他们的目标之类的内容。

sentences.en: I know they've made interoperability with C++ a very first-class feature in their world and much of their strategy.
sentences.zh: 我知道他们在自己的世界和大部分战略中，将与 C++ 的互操作性做成了一个非常核心的特性。

sentences.en: I think they have mentioned Swift's approach because they certainly know about us.
sentences.zh: 我想他们提到过 Swift 的方法，因为他们肯定知道我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But it's interesting because I think very few languages make this a priority or succeed in this way.
sentences.zh: 但这就很有趣了，因为我认为很少有语言会将此作为首要任务或以这种方式取得成功。

sentences.en: And we've talked in this podcast before about how hard it is for new languages to get off the ground.
sentences.zh: 我们以前在这个播客中讨论过新语言立足有多么困难。

sentences.en: And I am a big believer in the power of inertia.
sentences.zh: 而且我非常相信惯性的力量。

sentences.en: I like to say Bryce's rule of computing is that inertia is king.
sentences.zh: 我常说布莱斯的计算规则：惯性为王。

sentences.en: And we've talked about this rule of thumb that a language has to be
sentences.zh: 我们曾讨论过这样一个经验法则，即一门语言必须在

sentences.en: 10x better on some aspect to really break in.
sentences.zh: 某些方面好上 10 倍，才能真正打入市场。

sentences.en: But that's, I think, less true if you've got a great interoperability story.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有一个出色的互操作性方案，我想这就没那么绝对了。

sentences.en: And in fact, the interoperability can be the 10x improvement that, oh, wow, this is so easy for us to adopt and pick up and into migrate to something more modern.
sentences.zh: 事实上，互操作性可以成为那 10 倍的提升，让人觉得：哦，天哪，对我们来说采用、上手并迁移到更现代的东西是如此容易。

sentences.en: And we can do it incrementally.
sentences.zh: 而且我们可以循序渐进地做到这一点。

sentences.en: And that's how you get to the sort of rapid adoption that Swift's had.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Swift 获得这种迅猛采用的方式。

sentences.en: I'm not sure, Connor, if you have graphs or data to back this up.
sentences.zh: 康纳，我不确定你是否有图表或数据来支持这一点。

sentences.en: But my understanding is that Swift is what...
sentences.zh: 但我的理解是，Swift 在...

sentences.en: From when Swift was released to the first couple of years, it had very rapid growth trajectory relative to other new languages or languages that reached the scales that it has.
sentences.zh: 从 Swift 发布到最初的几年里，与其他新语言或达到同等规模的语言相比，它的增长轨迹非常迅猛。

sentences.en: Obviously, if you look at languages that go from zero to 1,000 users, that's not really a sample size that's sufficient to get the data.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你看那些从零增长到 1,000 名用户的语言，样本量其实不足以得出数据。

sentences.en: But if you're talking about going from zeros to millions of users, I don't think there's many of the languages that have done it as quickly as Swift has.
sentences.zh: 但如果你谈论的是从零增长到数百万用户，我认为没有多少语言能像 Swift 那样快地做到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that the language I would say is most similar in sort of rollout strategy is probably TypeScript, because it did
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我要说在推广策略上最相似的语言可能是 TypeScript，因为它做了

sentences.en: very much the same thing of there was a JavaScript ecosystem, which is massive.
sentences.zh: 非常相似的事情，当时有一个庞大的 JavaScript 生态系统。

sentences.en: It provided interoperability and a much better programming experience for that ecosystem and enjoyed very fast adoption.
sentences.zh: 它为该生态系统提供了互操作性和好得多的编程体验，并受到了非常快速的采用。

sentences.en: Well, I was just going to say there's a website.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正要说这里有个网站。

sentences.en: We'll leave a link.
sentences.zh: 我们会留一个链接。

sentences.en: I think you can hyperlink exact sort of customizations of what you select.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以对你选择的精确自定义内容进行超链接。

sentences.en: And it's called language and it's based on GitHub statistics.
sentences.zh: 它叫做 language，是基于 GitHub 统计数据的。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's all of these ranking things are taken with a huge grain of salt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，所有这些排名数据都得大打折扣来看待。

sentences.en: But if you actually look at TypeScript versus Swift from the period of like 2012, which is when this site goes back to 2016, 17, TypeScript is...
sentences.zh: 但如果你实际查看 TypeScript 与 Swift 从 2012 年（这个网站数据追溯到的时间）到 2016、17 年的对比，TypeScript...

sentences.en: They've got similar curves at first, but then something happened in 2014 and then Swift just takes off.
sentences.zh: 它们一开始的曲线很相似，但接着在 2014 年发生了某些变化，然后 Swift 就腾飞了。

sentences.en: And according to these stats actually was higher ranked than TypeScript up until 2017.
sentences.zh: 根据这些统计数据，实际上直到 2017 年，它的排名都比 TypeScript 要高。

sentences.en: And then 2017, I think, you know, TypeScript is slowly taking over the JavaScript world.
sentences.zh: 然后在 2017 年，我想，你知道的，TypeScript 正在慢慢接管 JavaScript 世界。

sentences.en: But yeah, like there's this period of two, two and a half years where Swift is...
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，就像有两到两年半的时间，Swift...

sentences.en: It's growing at this incredible rate, even faster than TypeScript at the time.
sentences.zh: 它以惊人的速度增长，甚至比当时的 TypeScript 还要快。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Swift was introduced in 2014.
sentences.zh: 所以，Swift 是在 2014 年推出的。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以...

sentences.en: Well, I have no idea what the data prior to 2014 is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我完全不知道 2014 年之前的数据是什么样的。

sentences.en: So, that's...
sentences.zh: 所以，那是...

sentences.en: It says that in 2013 Q4, in 2013 Q3, it does have some numbers.
sentences.zh: 上面说在 2013 年第四季度，在 2013 年第三季度，它确实有一些数字。

sentences.en: So, I don't know what that's from.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道这是从哪来的。

sentences.en: So, here's a possible theory.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一个可能的理论。

sentences.en: You said it's from GitHub data, right?
sentences.zh: 你刚才说它来自 GitHub 数据，对吧？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, it's possible that the Swift projects GitHub, Git history is now on GitHub.
sentences.zh: 所以，有可能 Swift 项目在 GitHub 上的 Git 历史现在已经放到 GitHub 上了。

sentences.en: Oh, it's public.
sentences.zh: 哦，它是公开的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And that it's looking at stuff from before it was publicly released.
sentences.zh: 而且它正在查看公开发布之前的内容。

sentences.en: So, that's probably...
sentences.zh: 所以，那可能...

sentences.en: The Swift compiler projects Git history goes all the way back to the dawn of time, which obviously predates when we launched it.
sentences.zh: Swift 编译器的 Git 历史可以追溯到很久很久以前，这显然早于我们发布它的时间。

sentences.en: So, that's probably where it comes from, but you would have a small number of users at that point.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能就是它的来源，但在那个时候你的用户数量会很少。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, one other thing that I think of when I think of Swift is I think of it as a teaching or an education language.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我想到 Swift 时，我脑海中浮现的另一件事是，我认为它是一门教学或教育语言。

sentences.en: And even from the launch of Swift, there has been a big focus on education, not just of programmers, but of people who are learning to program for the first time.
sentences.zh: 甚至从 Swift 推出之日起，人们就非常关注教育，不仅是针对程序员，还针对第一次学习编程的人。

sentences.en: Not just of career professional programmers who already know another language, but as a first
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是那些已经精通另一种语言的职业程序员，而是将其作为人们的

sentences.en: language for people, like when I think of first languages to recommend to people, Swift's often one that comes to mind.
sentences.zh: 第一门语言。比如当我想向人们推荐第一门语言时，Swift 常常是浮现在脑海中的选择之一。

sentences.en: Was that a focus from the start?
sentences.zh: 这从一开始就是重点吗？

sentences.en: How did that come to be?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: So, I think it follows from one of our philosophical points.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这符合我们的哲学观点之一。

sentences.en: So, we believe very deeply in this notion of progressive disclosure, the idea that when you're starting out, things should be simple and straightforward.
sentences.zh: 我们非常坚信渐进式披露的概念，即当你刚开始时，事情应该是简单直接的。

sentences.en: And as you grow, you start to need more capabilities.
sentences.zh: 随着你的成长，你开始需要更多的功能。

sentences.en: Those capabilities should be there and you can go learn about them, incorporate them.
sentences.zh: 这些功能应该在那里，你可以去了解并将其融入其中。

sentences.en: But there's two sort of buts.
sentences.zh: 但这里有两个类似“但是”的东西。

sentences.en: They shouldn't, first of all, they shouldn't come to you way too early.
sentences.zh: 首先，它们不应该过早地出现。

sentences.en: So, you shouldn't be forced to deal with a super advanced feature just because, you know, you step slightly outside of the bounds.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不应该仅仅因为你稍微越界了一点，就被迫去处理一个超级高级的特性。

sentences.en: And the other part is, it shouldn't invalidate anything that you've learned so far.
sentences.zh: 另一个部分是，它不应该使你迄今为止学到的任何东西失效。

sentences.en: And so, we do care a lot about the hello world experience, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实非常关心 Hello World 的体验，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you print hello world and it works.
sentences.zh: 比如你打印 Hello World，它就能运行。

sentences.en: And so, that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Like, just print and then earn quotes.
sentences.zh: 比如，只需用 print 然后加上引号。

sentences.en: Hello world is fine.
sentences.zh: Hello World 就很好。

sentences.en: And we want it to be fairly simple to then grow into doing simple data structures and building, you know, your own types with structs and enums and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它能足够简单，进而发展到能够处理简单的数据结构，并用结构体、枚举等构建你自己的类型。

sentences.en: And we do like that it can be used as a learning language.
sentences.zh: 我们确实喜欢它能被用作一门学习语言。

sentences.en: I think it is valuable that people can learn a language and it can grow with them, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为人们能够学习一门语言并且它能与他们共同成长，这很有价值，对吧？

sentences.en: So, when they're ready, they can say, you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以当他们准备好时，他们会说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I want to learn about generic programming.
sentences.zh: 我想了解泛型编程。

sentences.en: You know, Swift has a generic system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Swift 有一个泛型系统。

sentences.en: And, you know, the fun part about that is you can go and learn about generics and you write
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中有趣的部分是你可以去了解泛型，然后编写

sentences.en: your identity functions and you learn how to write a protocol, which is basically Swift speak for a concept.
sentences.zh: 你的恒等函数，并且你学习如何编写协议，这基本上就是 Swift 中对概念的称呼。

sentences.en: And you write some generic algorithMs. And then you realize that you've been using generics
sentences.zh: 你编写一些泛型算法。然后你意识到你一直在使用泛型

sentences.en: in your entire Swift existence because array is just a generic type defined in the library.
sentences.zh: 贯穿你的整个 Swift 生态，因为数组只是库中定义的一个泛型类型。

sentences.en: And you've been writing like filter and map operations on arrays as part of, you know, just writing code.
sentences.zh: 而且你一直在编写数组上的 filter 和 map 操作，作为你编写代码的一部分。

sentences.en: And those are simply generic algorithms that are expressed in the library on like the collection protocol.
sentences.zh: 这些只是在库中针对集合协议等表达的简单泛型算法。

sentences.en: And so, it was always there, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它一直都在，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this underlying more complex model was always there, but you weren't forced to confront it until later.
sentences.zh: 这种底层更复杂的模型一直都在，但直到后来你才被迫去面对它。

sentences.en: And this is tricky.
sentences.zh: 这很棘手。

sentences.en: Like, you know, we started talking about separate type checking with generics, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，我们开始讨论带泛型的独立类型检查，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to have that down solid, right?
sentences.zh: 你必须把这一点彻底搞懂，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's nothing that kills progressive disclosure worse than something like a template instance.
sentences.zh: 因为没有什么比模板实例之类的事情更能扼杀渐进式披露了。

sentences.en: You can backtrace, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以回溯，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That just throws you into all the complexity.
sentences.zh: 那会直接把你带入所有的复杂性之中。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you can keep it sort of there, but not required, you can have a language
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果你能让它既存在又不是必需的，你就可以拥有一门语言

sentences.en: that is both, you know, complex to model all the complicated scenarios that we need when we're doing
sentences.zh: 它既能模拟我们在进行诸如

sentences.en: like, you know, full on software engineering, but still keep it simple and approachable enough.
sentences.zh: 全面软件工程时所需的所有复杂场景，同时又能保持足够简单和易用。

sentences.en: Well, and there's also the fact that it is so great for programming like GUIs and apps and integrates
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有一个事实是它非常适合编写图形用户界面（GUI）和应用程序，并且与 Apple 框架

sentences.en: so nicely with the Apple frameworks, I think makes it a really good teaching language, especially for like kids.
sentences.zh: 集成得如此完美，我认为这使它成为一门非常好的教学语言，特别适合像小孩子这样的人。

sentences.en: And there's the, is it called Swift Playgrounds or something like that?
sentences.zh: 还有一个叫什么 Swift Playgrounds 还是类似名字的东西？

sentences.en: What's the name of the thing, the app on?
sentences.zh: 那个东西、那个应用程序叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, the Swift Playgrounds app lets you learn Swift on an iPad.
